plan: With three bidders in a second-price-style auction (the ascending clock effectively implements second-price mechanics), bidding my true value is the dominant strategy. My value is $4, which is quite low. Bidding truthfully ensures I only win when profitable (i.e., when the second-highest bid is below my value), and I never overpay since I'd pay the second-highest bid, not my own. There's no incentive to shade my bid up or down in this format.

This mechanism is equivalent to a second-price (Vickrey) auction: my sealed bid sets my exit price, and the winner pays the second-highest bid. In such auctions, truthful bidding is a dominant strategy—bidding above value risks overpaying, bidding below value risks losing profitable wins. Since I have no history to suggest otherwise and this is a one-shot game, the optimal action is to bid exactly my private value of $23 to maximize expected profit.

Since this auction functions like a second-price auction (the winner pays the second-highest bid/exit price), the dominant strategy is to bid my true value. Bidding exactly $32 ensures I win whenever the prize is worth more to me than to competitors, and I pay only the second-highest bid, which will always be at or below my value—guaranteeing non-negative profit if I win. Bidding higher risks overpaying; bidding lower risks losing profitable auctions.
